stories.headline: Saudi Arabia drives Gulf diplomatic effort to restrain US-Iran war and secure ceasefire deal
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan conducted an intensive week of diplomacy—phone calls with counterparts in Qatar, Egypt, Syria, Kuwait, Portugal, Nepal, Iran, and others—publicly praising Trump's decision to pause strikes on Iran and urging Tehran to seize the diplomatic opening. Crown Prince MBS was also cited by Trump as among the Gulf leaders who personally asked him to hold off on imminent bombing. Saudi Arabia's mediating posture was prominent in global coverage of the US-Iran conflict.

stories.headline: NEOM halts The Line construction until after 2030, cancels high-speed rail contract
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's NEOM megaproject formally halted further construction on The Line—a 170-kilometre dual-skyscraper city once projected to cost over $1 trillion—until at least 2030, and simultaneously terminated a €1.4 billion high-speed rail contract with Italy's Webuild with 20% of the work complete. NEOM is pivoting to develop Oxagon as a data-centre hub, with its 2030 population target revised down dramatically to 100,000 from a stated 9 million.

stories.headline: Drone attacks launched from Iraqi airspace intercept Saudi Arabia, testing Gulf security
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Defense announced on May 17 that air defense forces intercepted and destroyed three drones entering its airspace from Iraq, warning it reserves the right to respond. Iraq denied knowledge of launches from its territory and initiated investigations. Saudi Arabia and Kuwait condemned the attacks, and the GCC declared Saudi security inseparable from collective Gulf security. A separate drone attack on UAE's Barakah nuclear plant complex from Iraq on May 19 drew Saudi condemnation.

stories.headline: Pakistan secretly deploys 8,000 troops and fighter jets to Saudi Arabia under defence pact
stories.summary: Reuters reported exclusively that Pakistan has deployed approximately 8,000 troops, a squadron of JF-17 fighter aircraft, and a Chinese-origin HQ-9 air defense system to Saudi Arabia under a confidential mutual defence agreement signed last year. The pact reportedly provides for up to 80,000 Pakistani troops if needed to protect the Kingdom. The deployment is notable given Pakistan is simultaneously playing a diplomatic mediation role in the US-Iran conflict.

stories.headline: Aramco and Pasqal launch Saudi Arabia's first quantum computer and regional QCaaS platform
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco, in partnership with French quantum computing firm Pasqal, officially inaugurated Saudi Arabia's first quantum computer—a 200-qubit system housed at Aramco's Dhahran data center—and launched the Middle East's first commercial Quantum Computing as a Service (QCaaS) platform. Planned applications include port logistics optimization, CO2 storage, and well placement. Aramco's venture capital arm Wa'ed Ventures had invested in Pasqal in 2023.

stories.headline: PIF withdraws from LIV Golf as AI subsidiary HUMAIN signs McKinsey and Accenture
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund confirmed it would end funding for LIV Golf after the 2026 season following an estimated $5–8 billion investment since 2022, with PIF Governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan stepping down as LIV chairman. LIV is now seeking $350 million in new investment with a reduced 10-event schedule and player equity stakes. The same week, PIF's AI subsidiary HUMAIN announced enterprise partnerships with McKinsey and Accenture, signaling a strategic reorientation from sports soft power to domestic technology.

stories.headline: Hajj 2026 season begins with Saudi military deployment around Mecca, record pilgrim arrivals
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia deployed air defense missile systems around Mecca ahead of the 2026 Hajj season, with the Ministry of Defense releasing a comprehensive operational plan involving land, air, naval, and medical forces across 41 locations. Saudi Arabia confirmed Eid al-Adha dates for May 27, pilgrims from dozens of countries including Iraq, Iran, and Indonesia began arriving in large numbers, and various bilateral Hajj coordination meetings took place including between Indonesian police and Saudi Arabia's Presidency of State Security.

stories.headline: Saudi Cabinet chaired by King Salman affirms Kingdom will not hesitate to protect its security
stories.summary: King Salman chaired a Cabinet session in Jeddah in which the Council of Ministers formally reaffirmed that Saudi Arabia will take all measures necessary to protect its security, sovereignty, and citizens. The session also briefed ministers on Crown Prince MBS's phone calls with UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed and reportedly discussed regional developments including the Iran conflict. The statement was widely read as a signal in the context of ongoing drone attacks and Gulf tensions.

stories.headline: FairSquare report documents severe labor abuses of Nepali migrant workers in Aramco supply chain
stories.summary: Human rights group FairSquare released a report documenting 23 cases of alleged labor rights abuses among workers employed by Aramco's contractors and subcontractors in Saudi Arabia, including Nepali workers subjected to 12–14 hour shifts in temperatures above 50°C, passport confiscation, unsafe housing, and being denied compensation after serious injuries. The Guardian gave the report prominent coverage under the headline 'Aramco is selling our sweat and blood.'

stories.headline: Aramco Q1 2026 earnings show higher revenue and profit; Hormuz closure strains oil export logistics
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco reported higher revenue and profit in Q1 2026 supported by stronger crude prices, with its downstream EBIT sharply improving. Separately, CEO Amin Nasser warned publicly that if the Strait of Hormuz does not reopen by mid-June, global supply disruptions will persist into 2027, while noting Aramco could reach maximum 12 million bpd capacity within three weeks of reopening. The East-West pipeline had been operating at its 7 million bpd maximum throughout Q1.

stories.headline: GCC signs free trade agreement with United Kingdom after four years of negotiations
stories.summary: The Gulf Cooperation Council formally signed a free trade agreement with the United Kingdom in London, with GCC Secretary-General Jassim Al-Budaiwi and UK Trade Minister Chris Bryant signing the joint declaration. The deal covers over $53 billion in annual bilateral trade. Coverage appeared in Arabic-language regional media.

stories.summary: Seven principal OPEC+ member states are reported to be converging on a small increase in oil production targets for July—approximately 188,000 barrels per day—ahead of their June 7 meeting, despite ongoing disruptions to oil supply flows from the Iran war and partial Strait of Hormuz closure. Coverage appeared primarily in Arabic-language media.

stories.headline: UAE withdraws from OPEC to maximize oil output before energy transition, reshaping Gulf oil dynamics
stories.summary: UAE officials confirmed that Abu Dhabi's decision to withdraw from OPEC—announced weeks earlier—was the product of a three-year strategic study aimed at maximizing oil production revenues before the global energy transition. UAE diplomatic adviser Anwar Gargash stated the Emirates views itself as entering the 'autumn of the hydrocarbon age.' The move has strategic implications for Saudi Arabia's leadership of OPEC+.

stories.headline: Saudi March crude oil exports hit record low as Hormuz disruption forces East-West pipeline rerouting
stories.summary: JODI data showed Saudi Arabia's crude oil exports dropped to a record low of 4.974 million barrels per day in March 2026, the lowest since January 2002 data series began, as the Strait of Hormuz disruption forced rerouting through the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. Saudi Arabia also ramped up fuel oil imports by 86% year-on-year in April to substitute for declining gas output at power plants.

stories.headline: PIF raises $7 billion in record bond sale, trims US equity portfolio to $12 billion
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund completed its largest-ever single bond sale of $7 billion in May, drawing a $23.8 billion orderbook that was 3.4 times oversubscribed, suggesting bond markets are pricing in a de facto Saudi sovereign guarantee. Separately, PIF's Q1 2026 SEC filing showed it trimmed its US-listed equity holdings to approximately $12 billion, down from $12.9 billion at end-2025, while Saudi Treasury holdings surged to $160.4 billion in February—part of a broader domestic reorientation under Vision 2030.

stories.headline: King Salman International Airport construction advances with new contractor selections

MEED reported the airport development company selected three contractors for apron early contractor involvement. The project is central to Saudi Arabia's logistics strategy including a FedEx partnership.
